criteria.text: **A diagram is seen, not read.** For system-design answers the backend produces, what reaches the answer surface conveys structure visually. Define what you are measuring — nodes, edges, grouping, labels — register it before measuring the result, and show the supplied notebook diagrams and the product's output measured on the same scale.
**Nothing the backend expressed is lost on the way to the picture.** Every relation the answer states is present in what is shown. Measure it; do not assert it.

**It still fits and still reads.** The previous round's outcome holds, measured fresh: a typical answer's claim and beats are fully readable with nothing pressed; the overlay stays legible over any background with window opacity 1, an opaque local backing under every word, and zero contrast cost between 0% and 80% desktop visibility; no answer vanishes for being too long; panels replace the answer rather than clipping it.
**The candidate can still speak it.** A picture the operator cannot narrate is not an interview answer. Whatever you show, establish that the spoken form is still available and say where.
**What it costs is stated.** Rendering a diagram costs something — bytes shipped, time before the answer appears, screen area taken from the beats. Measure each and say who pays.
Distributions.: Every measurement carries observations, mean, median, the median's positional rank and spread; zero spread is stated explicitly when tied.
Aggregate influence.: Every aggregate carries per-item contribution, largest share, leave-one-out, and the smallest number of highest-contributing items whose removal flips the conclusion.
Before and after.: Rendered captures of the same answers before and after, in both languages.
Fail-before shown.: For every test added for this task, its failure against unchanged source is shown, not asserted.
Baseline quoted first.: The governing ship-setup record's failing identities are quoted before any failure is attributed.
Validation after the last write.: The complete output and direct exit code of every declared validation command, taken after the last write of the run.
